Sanger sequencing summary statistics and trees

Goals

What follows is our workflow for the general descriptive analysis of the Sanger sequencing data set for Zosterops. In this analysis we will describe the variation across our individual Sanger sequenced loci and construct trees for each of these loci using distance-based and maximum likelihood methods.

Getting started

We are using R version 4.4.2, RStudio version 2024.09.1 for the analysis. Quarto version 1.6.39 for Mac OS was used to document the workflow. Set the working directory in RStudio to one where the necessary phased Sanger sequencing alignments and other data are accessible.

Data files

This dataset includes Sanger sequenced polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplicon alignments for two mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and six protein coding nuclear loci (cdDNA). Prior to this analysis Sanger sequencing .ab1 files were uploaded to GeneiousⓇ 8.1.9 for editing, alignment, and quality control. Multiple sequencing runs for each amplicon were assembled and assembled loci were aligned across individual samples using Geneious Alignment. Alignments for each locus were trimmed and edited in Geneious and the identity of each locus confirmed with a megablast search. The reading frame was set by eye by avoiding frames with stop codons and a blastp search was done on the translation consensus for each alignment to confirm the locus identity. Alignments were exported as .fasta files.

Phase alignments of diploid cdDNA loci using PHASE 2.1.1 (Stephens, Smith, and Donnelly 2001). First, convert the alignment .fasta files from Geneious to the .inp format for PHASE 2.1.1 using the online SeqPHASE tool (Flot 2009). At the ‘Genotypes to be phased’ prompt click the ‘Browse’ button and select the appropriate .fasta alignment. Click the ‘Run SeqPHASE’ button. Once step 1 of the SeqPHASE process is completed retain the seqphase.const file in addition to the seqphase.inp file and rename each file appropriately to match the locus name (e.g. B3GNT9_seqphase.inp and B3GNT9_seqphase.const for locus B3GNT9).

Move the .inp from SeqPHASE to the directory with PHASE 2.1.1 and cd to that directory in the terminal. The .inp file is used to run the following PHASE 2.1.1 command in the terminal. For each locus <numberseed> should be replaced with an arbitrary number selected by the user and LOCUSNAME replaced with the designated name for that particular locus. Because each locus is relatively short chose the S option at the modeling flag (-M) as it assumes no within-locus recombination. Additional parameters are explained in the documentation for PHASE 2.1.1 available here.

./PHASE -MS -d1 -S<numberseed> -p0.85 -q0.85 -x5 -X10 LOCUSNAME_seqphase.inp LOCUSNAME_seqphase.out 5000 2 500

Further analysis will require FASTA alignments for each locus where each diploid individual contains two sequences corresponding to each of the two phased alleles determined in PHASE 2.1.1. Return to the online SeqPHASE tool and click the link to ‘step 2’. Select the appropriate .out file generated by the PHASE 2.1.1 run along with the matching .const file generated from step 1 in the SeqPHASE tool where prompted by a ‘Browse…’ button. The ‘Sort sequence’ box should be checked but the ‘Reduce sequences’ box should not be checked. Click the ‘Run SeqPHASE’ button and SeqPHASE will return a .fasta file with the complete sequence alignment and two phased haplotypes designated by the project number for that individual sample followed by a and b respectively. Click the ‘Click here to download the generated Fasta file’ link at the bottom of the page and rename the file to match the locus name. Including the .const file and unchecking the ‘Reduced sequences’ box will ensure the resulting FASTA file includes the full length of the alignment, not just the variable sites.

The phasing procedure was repeated for the following cdDNA FASTA alignments.

  • B3GNT9.fasta

  • BIRC2.fasta

  • CCDC.fasta

  • GPRC6.fasta

  • LACTBL.fasta

  • USP38.fasta

Subsequent analysis requires the following data files including those phased cdDNA alignments from the procedure described above.

  • COI.fasta

  • ND2.fasta

  • B3GNT9_phased.fasta

  • BIRC2_phased.fasta

  • CCDC_phased.fasta

  • GPRC6_phased.fasta

  • LACTBL_phased.fasta

  • USP38_phased.fasta

Description of summary statistics and tree building procedure for a single locus

Packages

Begin the analysis by restarting the R session (Session/Restart R in RStudio), loading the initial package libraries, and starting a log of the analysis. Other package libraries will be loaded as needed in later blocks. The following R packages should be installed using the Tools/Install Packages feature in RStudio.

  • logr (Bosak 2024) Optional if you wish to create a log file for the analysis.

  • ape (Paradis and Schliep 2019)

  • pegas (Paradis 2010)

  • phangorn (Schliep 2011)

  • gt (Iannone et al. 2024)

  • dplyr (Wickham et al. 2023)

Cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI)

Load and visualize the alignment

Estimate population genetic parameters

Nucleotide diversity

Calculate the nucleotide diversity for the locus.

# Nucleotide diversity
ndCOI <- nuc.div(ZosteropsCOI)
ndCOI
[1] 0.02057822

Haplotypes

Estimate the number of haplotypes and haplotype diversity.

# Number of haplotypes from phased DNA sequences (unique sequences) and hapotype diversity
hapCOI <- haplotype(ZosteropsCOI)
NumberHapsCOI <- nrow(hapCOI)
hapdivCOI <- hap.div(ZosteropsCOI)
hapCOI

Sequence length

Calculate sequence length.

# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthCOItotal <- length(ZosteropsCOI)
seqlengthCOI <- ncol(hapCOI)
lengthCOItotal
[1] 85272
seqlengthCOI
[1] 646

Number of sequences

Calculate the number of sequences in the alignment. Diploid phased cdDNA loci will have two sequences per individual sample and haploid mtDNA loci will have a single sequence per locus.

# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesCOI1 <- lengthCOItotal/seqlengthCOI
SummaryCOIlength <- unlist(strsplit(summaryCOI[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesCOI2 <- as.numeric(SummaryCOIlength)
all.equal(NumberSequencesCOI1, NumberSequencesCOI2)
[1] TRUE
NumberSequencesCOI1
[1] 132
NumberSequencesCOI2
[1] 132

𝛉 estimates

Estimate 𝛉 per locus, 𝛉 per site, and 𝛉 variance based on the the number of segregating sites (theta.s) and also estimate 𝛉 per locus based on the number of alleles (theta.k).

# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaCOIperLocusW <- theta.s(sCOI, NumberSequencesCOI1)
ThetaCOIperSiteW <- ThetaCOIperLocusW/seqlengthCOI
ThetaCOIperLocusVarW <- theta.s(sCOI, NumberSequencesCOI1, variance = TRUE)
ThetaCOIperLocusVarW <- ThetaCOIperLocusVarW[2]
ThetaCOIk <- theta.k(n = 132, k = 52)
ThetaCOIperLocusW

Tajima’s D and R2 tests

Test for potential deviations from neutrality using Tajima’s D (Tajima 1989) and population growth from the Ramos-Onsins and Roza’s test (Ramos-Onsins and Rozas 2002).

# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaCOI <- tajima.test(ZosteropsCOI)
R2COI <- R2.test(ZosteropsCOI,B = 10000, theta = ThetaCOIperLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

Trees

Distance-based trees

Unweighted pair group method with arithmetic mean (UPGMA) and neighbor joining (NJ) distance-based trees.

#UPGMA and NJ trees
dmCOI <- dist.ml(ZosteropsCOI)
UPGMAtreeCOI <- upgma(dmCOI)
NJtreeCOI <- NJ(dmCOI)
plot(UPGMAtreeCOI, main = "UPGMA COI", cex = 3)
plot(NJtreeCOI, "unrooted", main = "NJ COI", cex = 3)

Maximum likelihood trees

Maximum likelihood (ML) trees rooted either on the midpoint or an outgroup.

#ML tree midpoint and outgroup rooted trees
mtCOI <- modelTest(ZosteropsCOI)

Summary statistics

# Nucleotide diversity
ndND2 <- nuc.div(ZosteropsND2)
# Number of haplotypes from phased DNA sequences (unique sequences) and hapotype diversity
hapND2 <- haplotype(ZosteropsND2)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsND2): some sequences of different lengths
were assigned to the same haplotype
NumberHapsND2 <- nrow(hapND2)
hapdivND2 <- hap.div(ZosteropsND2)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences of different lengths were
assigned to the same haplotype
# An index of segregating sites and number of segregating sites 
seg.sitesND2 <- seg.sites(ZosteropsND2)
sND2 <- length(seg.sitesND2)
# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthND2total <- length(ZosteropsND2)
seqlengthND2 <- ncol(hapND2)
# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesND21 <- lengthND2total/seqlengthND2
SummaryND2length <- unlist(strsplit(summaryND2[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesND22 <- as.numeric(SummaryND2length)
all.equal(NumberSequencesND21, NumberSequencesND22)
[1] TRUE
# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaND2perLocusW <- theta.s(sND2, NumberSequencesND21)
ThetaND2perSiteW <- ThetaND2perLocusW/seqlengthND2
ThetaND2perLocusVarW <- theta.s(sND2, NumberSequencesND21, variance = TRUE)
ThetaND2perLocusVarW <- ThetaND2perLocusVarW[2]
# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaND2 <- tajima.test(ZosteropsND2)
R2ND2 <- R2.test(ZosteropsND2,B = 10000, theta = ThetaND2perLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

# Nucleotide diversity
ndB3GNT9 <- nuc.div(ZosteropsB3GNT9)
# Number of haplotypes from phased DNA sequences (unique sequences) and hapotype diversity
hapB3GNT9 <- haplotype(ZosteropsB3GNT9)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsB3GNT9): some sequences of different
lengths were assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsB3GNT9): some sequences were not assigned
to the same haplotype because of ambiguities
NumberHapsB3GNT9 <- nrow(hapB3GNT9)
hapdivB3GNT9 <- hap.div(ZosteropsB3GNT9)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences of different lengths were
assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences were not assigned to the same
haplotype because of ambiguities
# An index of segregating sites and number of segregating sites 
seg.sitesB3GNT9 <- seg.sites(ZosteropsB3GNT9)
sB3GNT9 <- length(seg.sitesB3GNT9)
# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthB3GNT9total <- length(ZosteropsB3GNT9)
seqlengthB3GNT9 <- ncol(hapB3GNT9)
# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesB3GNT91 <- lengthB3GNT9total/seqlengthB3GNT9
SummaryB3GNT9length <- unlist(strsplit(summaryB3GNT9[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesB3GNT92 <- as.numeric(SummaryB3GNT9length)
all.equal(NumberSequencesB3GNT91, NumberSequencesB3GNT92)
[1] TRUE
# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaB3GNT9perLocusW <- theta.s(sB3GNT9, NumberSequencesB3GNT91)
ThetaB3GNT9perSiteW <- ThetaB3GNT9perLocusW/seqlengthB3GNT9
ThetaB3GNT9perLocusVarW <- theta.s(sB3GNT9, NumberSequencesB3GNT91, variance = TRUE)
ThetaB3GNT9perLocusVarW <- ThetaB3GNT9perLocusVarW[2]
# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaB3GNT9 <- tajima.test(ZosteropsB3GNT9)
R2B3GNT9 <- R2.test(ZosteropsB3GNT9,B = 10000, theta = ThetaB3GNT9perLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

outgroupB3GNT9 <- c("ZAsu001a","ZAsu001b","ZAsu002a", "ZAsu002b")
mlB3GNT9root <- root(mlB3GNT9, outgroup = outgroupB3GNT9)
plot(mlB3GNT9root, show.node.label = TRUE, p = 50, type="p", main="Maximum Likelihood rooted on outgroup", cex = 3)

Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences of different lengths were

# An index of segregating sites and number of segregating sites 
seg.sitesBIRC2 <- seg.sites(ZosteropsBIRC2)
sBIRC2 <- length(seg.sitesBIRC2)
# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthBIRC2total <- length(ZosteropsBIRC2)
seqlengthBIRC2 <- ncol(hapBIRC2)
# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesBIRC21 <- lengthBIRC2total/seqlengthBIRC2
SummaryBIRC2length <- unlist(strsplit(summaryBIRC2[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesBIRC22 <- as.numeric(SummaryBIRC2length)
all.equal(NumberSequencesBIRC21, NumberSequencesBIRC22)
[1] TRUE
# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaBIRC2perLocusW <- theta.s(sBIRC2, NumberSequencesBIRC21)
ThetaBIRC2perSiteW <- ThetaBIRC2perLocusW/seqlengthBIRC2
ThetaBIRC2perLocusVarW <- theta.s(sBIRC2, NumberSequencesBIRC21, variance = TRUE)
ThetaBIRC2perLocusVarW <- ThetaBIRC2perLocusVarW[2]
# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaBIRC2 <- tajima.test(ZosteropsBIRC2)
R2BIRC2 <- R2.test(ZosteropsBIRC2,B = 10000, theta = ThetaBIRC2perLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

# An index of segregating sites and number of segregating sites 
seg.sitesCCDC <- seg.sites(ZosteropsCCDC)
sCCDC <- length(seg.sitesCCDC)
# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthCCDCtotal <- length(ZosteropsCCDC)
seqlengthCCDC <- ncol(hapCCDC)
# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesCCDC1 <- lengthCCDCtotal/seqlengthCCDC
SummaryCCDClength <- unlist(strsplit(summaryCCDC[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesCCDC2 <- as.numeric(SummaryCCDClength)
all.equal(NumberSequencesCCDC1, NumberSequencesCCDC2)
[1] TRUE
# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaCCDCperLocusW <- theta.s(sCCDC, NumberSequencesCCDC1)
ThetaCCDCperSiteW <- ThetaCCDCperLocusW/seqlengthCCDC
ThetaCCDCperLocusVarW <- theta.s(sCCDC, NumberSequencesCCDC1, variance = TRUE)
ThetaCCDCperLocusVarW <- ThetaCCDCperLocusVarW[2]
# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaCCDC <- tajima.test(ZosteropsCCDC)
R2CCDC <- R2.test(ZosteropsCCDC,B = 10000, theta = ThetaCCDCperLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

# Nucleotide diversity
ndGPRC6 <- nuc.div(ZosteropsGPRC6)
# Number of haplotypes from phased DNA sequences (unique sequences) and hapotype diversity
hapGPRC6 <- haplotype(ZosteropsGPRC6)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsGPRC6): some sequences of different
lengths were assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsGPRC6): some sequences were not assigned
to the same haplotype because of ambiguities
NumberHapsGPRC6 <- nrow(hapGPRC6)
hapdivGPRC6 <- hap.div(ZosteropsGPRC6)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences of different lengths were
assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences were not assigned to the same
haplotype because of ambiguities
# An index of segregating sites and number of segregating sites 
seg.sitesGPRC6 <- seg.sites(ZosteropsGPRC6)
sGPRC6 <- length(seg.sitesGPRC6)
# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthGPRC6total <- length(ZosteropsGPRC6)
seqlengthGPRC6 <- ncol(hapGPRC6)
# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesGPRC61 <- lengthGPRC6total/seqlengthGPRC6
SummaryGPRC6length <- unlist(strsplit(summaryGPRC6[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesGPRC62 <- as.numeric(SummaryGPRC6length)
all.equal(NumberSequencesGPRC61, NumberSequencesGPRC62)
[1] TRUE
# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaGPRC6perLocusW <- theta.s(sGPRC6, NumberSequencesGPRC61)
ThetaGPRC6perSiteW <- ThetaGPRC6perLocusW/seqlengthGPRC6
ThetaGPRC6perLocusVarW <- theta.s(sGPRC6, NumberSequencesGPRC61, variance = TRUE)
ThetaGPRC6perLocusVarW <- ThetaGPRC6perLocusVarW[2]
# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaGPRC6 <- tajima.test(ZosteropsGPRC6)
R2GPRC6 <- R2.test(ZosteropsGPRC6,B = 10000, theta = ThetaGPRC6perLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

bsGPRC6 <- bootstrap.pml(fit_mtGPRC6, bs = 100, optNni = TRUE, control = pml.control(trace = 0))
mlGPRC6 <- plotBS(midpoint(fit_mtGPRC6$tree), bsGPRC6, show.node.label = TRUE, p = 50, type="p", main="Maximum likelihood midpoint rooted standard bootstrap", cex = 3)
outgroupGPRC6 <- c("ZAsu001b","ZAsu002b")

plot(mlGPRC6root, show.node.label = TRUE, p = 50, type="p", main="Maximum Likelihood rooted on outgroup", cex = 3)

Summary statistics

# Nucleotide diversity
ndLACTBL <- nuc.div(ZosteropsLACTBL)
# Number of haplotypes from phased DNA sequences (unique sequences) and hapotype diversity
hapLACTBL <- haplotype(ZosteropsLACTBL)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsLACTBL): some sequences of different
lengths were assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsLACTBL): some sequences were not assigned
to the same haplotype because of ambiguities
NumberHapsLACTBL <- nrow(hapLACTBL)
hapdivLACTBL <- hap.div(ZosteropsLACTBL)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences of different lengths were
assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences were not assigned to the same
haplotype because of ambiguities
# An index of segregating sites and number of segregating sites 
seg.sitesLACTBL <- seg.sites(ZosteropsLACTBL)
sLACTBL <- length(seg.sitesLACTBL)
# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthLACTBLtotal <- length(ZosteropsLACTBL)
seqlengthLACTBL <- ncol(hapLACTBL)
# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesLACTBL1 <- lengthLACTBLtotal/seqlengthLACTBL
SummaryLACTBLlength <- unlist(strsplit(summaryLACTBL[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesLACTBL2 <- as.numeric(SummaryLACTBLlength)
all.equal(NumberSequencesLACTBL1, NumberSequencesLACTBL2)
[1] TRUE
# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaLACTBLperLocusW <- theta.s(sLACTBL, NumberSequencesLACTBL1)
ThetaLACTBLperSiteW <- ThetaLACTBLperLocusW/seqlengthLACTBL
ThetaLACTBLperLocusVarW <- theta.s(sLACTBL, NumberSequencesLACTBL1, variance = TRUE)
ThetaLACTBLperLocusVarW <- ThetaLACTBLperLocusVarW[2]
# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaLACTBL <- tajima.test(ZosteropsLACTBL)
R2LACTBL <- R2.test(ZosteropsLACTBL,B = 10000, theta = ThetaLACTBLperLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

bsLACTBL <- bootstrap.pml(fit_mtLACTBL, bs = 100, optNni = TRUE, control = pml.control(trace = 0))
mlLACTBL <- plotBS(midpoint(fit_mtLACTBL$tree), bsLACTBL, show.node.label = TRUE, p = 50, type="p", main="Maximum likelihood midpoint rooted standard bootstrap", cex = 3)
outgroupLACTBL <- c("ZAsu002a","ZAsu002b")
mlLACTBLroot <- root(mlLACTBL, outgroup = outgroupLACTBL)
plot(mlLACTBLroot, show.node.label = TRUE, p = 50, type="p", main="Maximum Likelihood rooted on outgroup", cex = 3)

Summary statistics

# Nucleotide diversity
ndUSP38 <- nuc.div(ZosteropsUSP38)
# Number of haplotypes from phased DNA sequences (unique sequences) and hapotype diversity
hapUSP38 <- haplotype(ZosteropsUSP38)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsUSP38): some sequences of different
lengths were assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(ZosteropsUSP38): some sequences were not assigned
to the same haplotype because of ambiguities
NumberHapsUSP38 <- nrow(hapUSP38)
hapdivUSP38 <- hap.div(ZosteropsUSP38)
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences of different lengths were
assigned to the same haplotype
Warning in haplotype.DNAbin(x): some sequences were not assigned to the same
haplotype because of ambiguities
# An index of segregating sites and number of segregating sites 
seg.sitesUSP38 <- seg.sites(ZosteropsUSP38)
sUSP38 <- length(seg.sitesUSP38)
# Total length of all sequences (number of sequences x sequence length) and sequence length
lengthUSP38total <- length(ZosteropsUSP38)
seqlengthUSP38 <- ncol(hapUSP38)
# Number of sequences calulated two ways, by divdiding the total length by the sequence length (calculation 1) and by extracting the length value from the summary (caclulation 2)
# Confirm both calculations for number of sequences are the same
NumberSequencesUSP381 <- lengthUSP38total/seqlengthUSP38
SummaryUSP38length <- unlist(strsplit(summaryUSP38[1,1], split = ":", fixed = TRUE))[2]
NumberSequencesUSP382 <- as.numeric(SummaryUSP38length)
all.equal(NumberSequencesUSP381, NumberSequencesUSP382)
[1] TRUE
# Calculate theta per sequence, theta per site, theta variance from the Watterson estimator based on number of segregating sites.
ThetaUSP38perLocusW <- theta.s(sUSP38, NumberSequencesUSP381)
ThetaUSP38perSiteW <- ThetaUSP38perLocusW/seqlengthUSP38
ThetaUSP38perLocusVarW <- theta.s(sUSP38, NumberSequencesUSP381, variance = TRUE)
ThetaUSP38perLocusVarW <- ThetaUSP38perLocusVarW[2]
# Tests for neutrality including Tajima's D and Ramos-Onsins and Roza's test
tajimaUSP38 <- tajima.test(ZosteropsUSP38)
R2USP38 <- R2.test(ZosteropsUSP38,B = 10000, theta = ThetaUSP38perLocusW, plot = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)

bsUSP38 <- bootstrap.pml(fit_mtUSP38, bs = 100, optNni = TRUE, control = pml.control(trace = 0))
mlUSP38 <- plotBS(midpoint(fit_mtUSP38$tree), bsUSP38, show.node.label = TRUE, p = 50, type="p", main="Maximum likelihood midpoint rooted standard bootstrap", cex = 3)
outgroupUSP38 <- c("ZAsu001a")
mlUSP38root <- root(mlUSP38, outgroup = outgroupUSP38)
plot(mlUSP38root, show.node.label = TRUE, p = 50, type="p", main="Maximum Likelihood rooted on outgroup", cex = 3)

Summary table for all loci

Load libraries

Create a table that summarizes the population genetic data across all loci. First, load the gt and dplyr package libraries.

library(gt)

    where
library(dplyr)

    intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

Create summary table

Create the summary table from the population genetic parameters estimated for each locus.

#Create table from estimates across all loci.
LocusNames <- c("COI","ND2", "B3GNT9", "BIRC2", "CCDC", "GPRC6", "LACTBL", "USP38")
LocusType <- c("mt", "mt", "cd", "cd", "cd", "cd", "cd", "cd")
NumberIndividuals <- c(NumberSequencesCOI1, NumberSequencesND21, NumberSequencesB3GNT91/2, NumberSequencesBIRC21/2, NumberSequencesCCDC1/2, NumberSequencesGPRC61/2, NumberSequencesLACTBL1/2, NumberSequencesUSP381/2)
NumberSequences <- c(NumberSequencesCOI1, NumberSequencesND21, NumberSequencesB3GNT91, NumberSequencesBIRC21, NumberSequencesCCDC1, NumberSequencesGPRC61, NumberSequencesLACTBL1, NumberSequencesUSP381)
SequenceLength <- c(seqlengthCOI, seqlengthND2, seqlengthB3GNT9, seqlengthBIRC2, seqlengthCCDC, seqlengthGPRC6, seqlengthLACTBL, seqlengthUSP38)
SegSites <- c(sCOI, sND2, sB3GNT9, sBIRC2, sCCDC, sGPRC6, sLACTBL, sUSP38)
NucleotideDiversity <- c(ndCOI, ndND2, ndB3GNT9, ndBIRC2, ndCCDC, ndGPRC6, ndLACTBL, ndUSP38)
NucleotideDiversity <- round(NucleotideDiversity, digits = 3)
NumberHaplotypes <- c(NumberHapsCOI, NumberHapsND2, NumberHapsB3GNT9, NumberHapsBIRC2, NumberHapsCCDC, NumberHapsGPRC6, NumberHapsLACTBL, NumberHapsUSP38)
HaplotypeDiversity <- c(hapdivCOI, hapdivND2, hapdivB3GNT9, hapdivBIRC2, hapdivCCDC, hapdivGPRC6, hapdivLACTBL, hapdivUSP38)
HaplotypeDiversity <- round(HaplotypeDiversity, digits = 2)
ThetaWperLocus <- c(ThetaCOIperLocusW, ThetaND2perLocusW, ThetaB3GNT9perLocusW, ThetaBIRC2perLocusW, ThetaCCDCperLocusW, ThetaGPRC6perLocusW, ThetaLACTBLperLocusW, ThetaUSP38perLocusW)
ThetaWperLocus <- round(ThetaWperLocus, digits = 2)
ThetaWvariance <- c(ThetaND2perLocusVarW, ThetaND2perLocusVarW, ThetaB3GNT9perLocusVarW, ThetaBIRC2perLocusVarW, ThetaCCDCperLocusVarW, ThetaGPRC6perLocusVarW, ThetaLACTBLperLocusVarW, ThetaUSP38perLocusVarW)
ThetaWvariance <- round(ThetaWvariance, digits = 2)
ThetaWperSite <- c(ThetaCOIperSiteW, ThetaND2perSiteW, ThetaB3GNT9perSiteW, ThetaBIRC2perSiteW, ThetaCCDCperSiteW, ThetaGPRC6perSiteW, ThetaLACTBLperSiteW, ThetaUSP38perSiteW)
ThetaWperSite <- round(ThetaWperSite, digits = 3)
Tajima <- c(tajimaCOI$D,tajimaND2$D, tajimaB3GNT9$D, tajimaBIRC2$D, tajimaCCDC$D, tajimaGPRC6$D, tajimaLACTBL$D, tajimaUSP38$D)
Tajima <- round(Tajima, digits = 2)
TajimaPValue <- c(tajimaCOI$Pval.normal,tajimaND2$Pval.normal, tajimaB3GNT9$Pval.normal, tajimaBIRC2$Pval.normal, tajimaCCDC$Pval.normal, tajimaGPRC6$Pval.normal, tajimaLACTBL$Pval.normal, tajimaUSP38$Pval.normal)
TajimaPValue <- round(TajimaPValue, digits = 3)
R2Test <- c(R2COI$R2, R2ND2$R2, R2B3GNT9$R2, R2BIRC2$R2, R2CCDC$R2, R2GPRC6$R2, R2LACTBL$R2, R2USP38$R2)
R2Test <- round(R2Test, digits = 2)
R2TestPValue <- c(R2COI$P.val, R2ND2$P.val, R2B3GNT9$P.val, R2BIRC2$P.val, R2CCDC$P.val, R2GPRC6$P.val, R2LACTBL$P.val, R2USP38$P.val)
R2TestPValue <- round(R2TestPValue, digits = 3)
AllLociSummary <- data.frame(LocusNames, LocusType, NumberIndividuals, NumberSequences, SequenceLength, SegSites, NucleotideDiversity, NumberHaplotypes, HaplotypeDiversity, ThetaWperLocus, ThetaWvariance, ThetaWperSite, Tajima, TajimaPValue, R2Test, R2TestPValue)
colnames(AllLociSummary) <- c("Locus", "Locus type", "Individuals", "Number of sequences", "Length", "Segregating sites", "\u03C0", "Number of haplotypes", "Haplotype diversity", "\u03B8 per locus", "\u03B8 per locus variance", "\u03B8 per site", "Tajima's D", "Tajima's D p-value", "R2 test", "R2 test p-value")

  tab_footnote(footnote = md("Locus type denoted as mitochondrial (mt) or nuclear protein coding (cd). For phased nuclear DNA alignments the number of sequences is 2x the number of individuals sequenced. \u03C0 is per site nucleotide diversity. Haplotype diversity calculated according to Nei and Tajima (1981). \u03B8 per locus and per locus variance in \u03B8 are estimated from the number of segregating sites (Watterson estimator). \u03B8 per site is calculated by dividing the \u03B8 per locus by the sequence length. Tajima's D and the Ramos-Onsins and Rozas (R2) tests are used to test for neutralilty and population growth, repsectively, at each locus. Population genetic parameters for each locus were estimated in the pegas and ape R packages"))

Haplotype diversity calculated according to Nei and Tajima (1981). θ per locus and per locus variance in θ are estimated from the number of segregating sites (Watterson estimator). θ per site is calculated by dividing the θ per locus by the sequence length.
